title: Scale a test shot to the press lane to set a spring kicker's stroke
instruction: Use the spring pusher to feed the blue blank under the guard so it stops in the green nest. A test blank from the same batch is on the left slide; the press lane drags 1.5 times as much.
context: Done by: press setters (O*NET 51-4031) trying out a die before stops are fitted. A spring kicker behind the guard sends each blank coasting into the die; how far it coasts depends on the batch's lubrication. The test slide shows how a batch slides, but the die lane drags 1.5 times as much. Unlike TK-6WAJ5C (practice rolls, then the same roll counted) and TK-8ERYTL (peel to an out-of-reach stone), the test lane differs, so its result must be scaled, not copied.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Two slide lanes (fixed, rigid), centred 12 cm left (test slide) and 12 cm right (press lane) of the midline, each running front to back from 23 to 65 cm in front of the arm bases: a light grey floor 420 mm long, 48 mm wide and 30 mm tall, with mid grey side walls 6 mm thick rising 24 mm above the floor (channel 36 mm wide). The nest is from 280 to 400 mm along each lane (51 to 63 cm in front). Spring pusher on each lane: a white pusher face 8 mm long, 28 mm wide and 12 mm tall, centred 9 mm above the floor (39 mm above the table), its front 70 mm along the lane at rest, on a white rod 8 mm square at the same height, ending in a black knob post 14 mm across and 42 mm tall (33 to 75 mm high) centred 20 mm behind the floor's near end. The knob pulls back toward the robot against a 100 N/m spring (moving mass 50 g, damping 0.3 N s/m), up to 80 mm; on release the face can run 15 mm past rest. Stroke scale beside each knob, on the side toward the midline: a white plate 100 x 20 x 2 mm on the table, centred 34 mm from the lane's centre line, from 110 to 10 mm behind the floor's near end (12 to 22 cm in front), with four ticks 3 mm wide across it: yellow (mark 1), orange (2), red (3), purple (4), where the knob is when pulled back 26.3, 32.3, 39.5 and 48.4 mm (each 1.225 times the last, so each stores 1.5 times the energy). Test slide: open; green caps 120 mm long, 16 mm wide and 2 mm thick on both wall tops, overhanging outward, mark its nest. Press lane: a dark grey guard roof 4 mm thick on its walls from 20 to 250 mm along the lane (25 to 48 cm in front); from there to the lane end, a dark grey slotted roof of two strips 19 mm wide and 4 mm thick on the walls, leaving a 10 mm slot along the centre line, with green strips 2 mm thick on both strips over the nest; two yellow light-curtain posts 12 mm square and 150 mm tall at 48.6 cm in front, 76 mm either side of the lane's centre line. A white plate 44 mm front to back, 64 mm wide and 2 mm thick, centred 33 cm in front and 18.2 cm right of the midline, reads 1.5 in black figures 28 mm tall (tops away from the robot). Scrap bins (fixed, dark red, open top and open toward the lane) under each lane's end, starting 4 mm past it: a 3 mm floor 86 mm front to back and 80 mm wide, with walls 30 mm tall and 4 mm thick on the far end and both sides, from 65.4 to 74 cm in front. Blanks (loose, rigid, blue, 30 g): 40 mm long, 30 mm wide, 15 mm tall, lying flat in each lane 2 mm in front of the pusher face (centre 32.2 cm in front). Lots change only the batch: the blanks' sliding friction on the test slide is lot A 0.18 (dry), lot B 0.08 (oiled), lot C 0.12 (lightly oiled); on the press lane it is always 1.5 times that (0.27, 0.12, 0.18). Both blanks look alike in every lot. Nothing else is on the table. Trials are run on lots A, B and C and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Pass/fail per trial. Score 0, judged over the whole trial from the video, if at any point any part of either arm crosses the light curtain: farther in front than the line of the yellow posts' near faces (48 cm in front) and between their inner faces (from 5 to 19 cm right of the midline), at any height. Otherwise score 1.0 when, at the end, the blue blank in the press lane lies flat (tilted at most 10 degrees) on the lane floor (its underside within 1.5 mm of the floor top), its whole length within the nest (51 to 63 cm in front, under the green strips), still for 1 s, with no gripper within 5 mm of it. Score 0 otherwise: stopped short, past the nest, in the scrap bin, or anywhere else. The test blank is not scored. Trials are run on each of lots A, B and C and averaged.
reset_notes: Push each knob back to rest (the spring does it). Set each blue blank flat in its lane, 2 mm in front of the pusher face. Lot A: dry blanks; lot B: oiled; lot C: lightly oiled (friction on the test slide 0.18, 0.08, 0.12; on the press lane 1.5 times that). Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 3 (trial k uses lot k mod 3).
fidelity: A bench mock-up of a die try-out feed. Each lot sets the blanks' friction in the simulator, and the press lane's is exactly 1.5 times the test slide's; a real lane's factor would be measured and less exact. The blanks look the same. The pusher strikes rigidly with no bounce. The slotted roof keeps fingers out of the nest; a scored light curtain backs it up. The lots stop a fixed stroke, not a memorised replay of all three.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A, B and C); demo: 1.0 in each lot
